Alyssa (ML): Heads-up — during the latest HF->Redwood bring-up for opt-2.7B we hit a subtle tool-calling tokenization problem.
Mike (Infra): ugh, details?
Alyssa (ML): When converting the HF chat templates we kept the HF special tokens (`<|tool_start|>`, `<|tool_end|>`) as-is. But tokenizer merges them weirdly after quantized ops.
Rahul (DevEx): Can you paste an example of the merge?
Alyssa (ML): Sure — root prompt: 
```
System: You are an assistant.
User: Run tool X with args -> <|tool_start|>{\"op\":\"search\",\"q\":\"redwood\"}<|tool_end|>
```
After tokenizing+quantize step the model sees `\"<|tool_start|>{\"op\":\"search\",...` as a single token boundary which breaks the runtime parser expecting distinct role tokens.
Lina (Eval): That would definitely break our JSON-mode extraction. We saw 8% failure on a small eval set.
Mike (Infra): Is this tokenizer-specific? Which HF tokenizer are we converting from?
Alyssa (ML): `tiktoken`-style BPE from HF's `tokenizer.json` (from community model). The config.json had `added_tokens` defined in a way that conflated `tool_start` and adjacent punctuation.
Rahul (DevEx): Two quick suggestions: 1) add explicit whitespace around tool markers in conversion. 2) register the special tokens as separate `added_tokens` entries with `single_word=false`.
Alyssa (ML): Tried both. Adding whitespace helped but is fragile for existing prompts. Marking as non-single-word works but some quantization kernels still fuse tokens for speed.
Mike (Infra): Could we switch to different delimiter tokens that are guaranteed to be reserved? e.g., `<<TOOL_START>>`?
Lina (Eval): That changes prompt templates and breaks backward compat with customers. Not ideal.
Alyssa (ML): We prototyped a runtime-layer solution: at request ingest, before detokenize, run a small splitter that enforces token boundaries for tool tags. Pseudocode: 
```
def protect_tags(text):
    return re.sub(r"(<\|tool_start\|>|<\|tool_end\|>)"," \\g<1> ", text)
```
This ensures tokenizers see spaces.
Rahul (DevEx): Nice. Could we instead canonicalize to Redwood's JSON-mode tokens? e.g., wrap tools with `<RWD_TOOL_START>` and `<RWD_TOOL_END>` in the internal format, then map back at output?
Alyssa (ML): Yeah that's what we landed on: conversion step maps HF tags -> Redwood guarded tokens, marks them in the config as `added_tokens` with `single_word=false`, and runtime enforces `protect_tags` idempotently.
Mike (Infra): Any perf hit?
Alyssa (ML): Minimal — the regex is cheap. Biggest risk was quantized kernel fusing during KV cache tokenization in generation. To mitigate, we inserted a tiny no-op byte escape `\uE000` between tag and JSON start when serializing internal tool calls; the byte is stripped before runtime parse.
Lina (Eval): Do we have eval results after the fix?
Alyssa (ML): Yes — on the Canary eval set: tool-calling success went from 92% -> 99.4%. Regression rate for normal chat decreased slightly (0.4%) due to extra whitespace but within threshold.
eval-bot: deploy-report: canary=opt-2.7b-quant-v3 | tool-call-success=99.4% | chat-regression=0.4% | notes="whitespace guard added"
Rahul (DevEx): We should document conversion rules in the devex guide and add a unit test that tokenizes common tool-call patterns before and after conversion.
Alyssa (ML): Agreed. I'll open a PR with: 1) conversion script snippet, 2) runtime protective layer, 3) eval results and testcases.
Mike (Infra): Also add a warning in console when a converted model's `config.json` has `added_tokens` that look merged (heuristic: tokens containing braces or quotes).
Lina (Eval): I'll add a regression suite for JSON-mode tokens and JSON parse accuracy.
Alyssa (ML): FYI — for HF models that use role tokens like `<|assistant|>` vs `assistant:` we added a small map in the conversion: role tokens -> Redwood role tags. That helped normalize chat templates across model variants.
Rahul (DevEx): Good. One more: function-calling schema expects top-level `tool_name` field. Some HF tool examples put it inside the `args` object. Our conversion flattens `args.tool` -> `tool_name`. Keep an eye on that during onboarding.
Alyssa (ML): Noted — I'll include a small schema-flatten step in the script.
Mike (Infra): Thanks — sounds actionable. Ping when PR is up and we'll canary the next build. :thumbsup:
Alyssa (ML): Will do. Thanks all.
Rahul (DevEx): Thanks — saved a bunch of head-scratching during rollout.
Lina (Eval): Adding testcases to the eval harness now.
eval-bot: reminder: please link PR to ticket INF-4023 for rollout tracking
